walkthroughs.body_html:
Speed depends on who is watching.

You walk down a moving train at 1 m/s. The train goes at 30 m/s.

Other passengers see you at 1 m/s. A person on the platform sees you at 31 m/s!

That's why scientists always say relative to what?

Average speed = total distance over total time. Smooths out the whole trip.

Instantaneous speed = speed right now, at this moment.

Your speedometer shows instantaneous speed.
Your satnav arrival time uses average speed.

Tricky problems: travel 60 km at 60 km/h, then 60 km at 30 km/h. What's the average?

It's not 45 - you spend longer at the slower speed!

Stage 1: 1 hour. Stage 2: 2 hours. Total: 120 km in 3 hours = 40 km/h.

Always use total distance / total time, never just average the speeds.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the activity of a source and the dose received by a person?
options: Activity and dose are the same — both measure how dangerous the radiation is.
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.
Activity is for nuclear power stations and dose is for medical X-rays.
Activity (Bq) is the rate of nuclear decays in the source; dose (Sv) measures the biological effect of absorbed radiation on tissue.

mcqs.q: When you push a wall, what does Newton's third law say about the wall?
options: The wall exerts an equal and opposite force on you at the same instant.
Activity is for nuclear power stations and dose is for medical X-rays.
The wall only pushes back if your force is strong enough to make it react.
The wall pushes back with a force proportional to how stiff it is, not equal to your force.
